First, let's factor the expression as a perfect square trinomial in ${x}^{2}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}+10{x}^{2}+25 & ={({x}^{2})}^{2}+2\cdot 5\cdot ({x}^{2})+{5}^{2} \\  & ={({x}^{2}+5)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to factor the sum of squares in the parentheses. To do this, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${i}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+5 & ={x}^{2}-(-5) \\  & ={x}^{2}-(5{i}^{2}) \\  & ={x}^{2}-{(\sqrt{5}\,i)}^{2} \\  & =(x+\sqrt{5}\,i)(x-\sqrt{5}\,i)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{4}+10{x}^{2}+25 & ={({x}^{2}+5)}^{2} \\  & ={((x+\sqrt{5}\,i)(x-\sqrt{5}\,i))}^{2} \\  & ={(x+\sqrt{5}\,i)}^{2}{(x-\sqrt{5}\,i)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
